newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Runway welcome for Italian force at Tirana airport.
newsitem.headline: Runway welcome for Italian force at Tirana airport.

text.p: Military transport aircraft swooped out of the sky shortly after dawn on Tuesday as Italian paratroopers on a historic mission to protect aid convoys landed in anarchic Albania.

Unlike a similar heavily-guarded landing at the main port of Durres, there was light security at Tirana airport where the 150 Italian paratroopers wearing red berets and heavy backpacks landed to beef up the operation to protect aid convoys.
There were no police checks on the narrow road leading into the airport and journalists were able to drive straight onto the modest landing strip.
Italian officers coming off the plane smiled and shook hands with the reporters.
An Albanian officer hurried over and ordered photographers to stop taking pictures and they were escorted away by Albanian soldiers carrying Kalashnikov rifles.

The paratroopers landing at Tirana airport were part of a force of nearly 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish troops who arrived in Albania on a mission to protect deliveries of emergency food and medicines to Albania's poor.

An armed insurrection in the Balkan country has claimed nearly 300 lives, with tens of thousands of weapons ending up in the hands of mafias and ordinary Albanians after raids on abandoned state armouries.
Sheep grazed on the runway as the six military aircraft landed within a few minutes of each other to deposit troops, jeeps and supplies at the landing strip outside the capital.
The main landing force began arriving on four naval vessels in the western port city of Durres just moments after the Italian aircraft carrying the paratroopers touched down.
A total of 6,000 troops from eight nations will arrive during the next two weeks on the mission to safeguard humanitarian aid convoys that has U.N. Security Council backing.
